narrative_purpose: Show that evolution can remove an appendage by switching off its developmental programme rather than degrading every limb gene: a python retains tiny pelvic spurs while a more derived snake carries no external trace, with intact internal patterning implied beneath both bodies.
subject: Two adult snakes presented side by side as anatomical specimens: a heavy-bodied python curled to expose two tiny paired pelvic spurs beside the cloaca, and a slender advanced snake with a completely smooth limbless underside; beneath the python's translucent skin, a small vestigial pelvic girdle and short internal femur remnants are visible, while a faint early-embryo inset shows paired limb buds beginning as small rounded swellings before disappearing later in development.
scene: A dark comparative anatomy plate with the adult bodies floating over a restrained translucent embryology inset, no written notation.
camera: Ventral three-quarter study view on the python pelvis and spurs, matched side view of the smooth-bodied snake, close enough for the vestiges to read clearly.
light: Cool raking specimen light catching scales and the tiny spurs, faint cyan transmitted light through the cutaway pelvis and embryo, deep indigo shadow around the bodies.
palette: Void indigo, desaturated olive and stone-grey scales, ocean-teal anatomy, Pandora cyan for translucent developmental tissue, one restrained ember accent at the vestigial pelvis.
style: Painterly evolutionary-anatomy naturalist plate, hand-painted, observational and precise rather than grotesque.
detail_level: High detail on the python's paired spurs, pelvic remnants, and embryonic limb buds; adult bodies soften into the dark away from the comparison zone.
composition: Python pelvis anchors the left half, the smooth advanced snake mirrors it on the right, and the small embryo curves below them in a dark central pocket.
consistency_notes: The python must have only the real tiny paired pelvic spurs, not functional feet. The comparison communicates lost developmental activation, not injured or amputated limbs.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no full legs on adult snakes, no dragon anatomy, no wounds or amputation, no horror, no photographic or glossy 3D render look, no cartoon or anime style
